newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran not to reschedule debts this year - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iran not to reschedule debts this year - MEES.

text.p: Iran will have no problems meeting its scheduled foreign debt repayments of more than $7 billion this year, its Central Bank governor said in remarks published on Monday.
"For the current year, definitely we do not see any problem and we think we can service our debt without any delay or default," Mohsen Nourbakhsh told the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES).
He was referring to the Iranian year which ends on March 20, 1998.
Nourbakhsh also said Iran would not need further rescheduling of its total foreign debt which he put at $13.7 billion in the long term and $5.1 billion in the short term.
"There is no need for rescheduling and the story of rescheduling in our economic history is finished," Nourbakhsh said.
Central Bank figures earlier this year showed rescheduled repayment obligations at $7.15 billion in 1997-98. Higher than expected revenues from oil receipts are being channeled into debt repayments.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said in December that Iran had no trouble then servicing its debts following a a series of bilateral reschedulings.
